title: Institutional Funding Partnership Map
placeholder: Click any need or partner. The two nodes with more than one line are the ones worth looking at.

nodes.label:
Multi-Year
Recurring Cash
detail: The need
Money the club can count on for more than one year, so a budget can be planned rather than re-fought every September.
Why it is hard
Almost every one-time channel from Chapter 30 -- a bake sale, a crowdfunder, a single grant -- funds one year and leaves the next year open.
Worked figure
The sample club's $830 of recurring costs is exactly what this need has to cover, every year, indefinitely.

nodes.label:
Free or Discounted
Meeting Space
detail: The need
Somewhere to meet that does not appear as a line in the budget.
Why it matters most
Venue hire is usually the largest single recurring cost a club can eliminate outright, and the only one that can go to zero rather than merely down.
Note
The only need on this map with two partners able to address it -- see both edges leaving this node.

nodes.label:
Renewable Annual
Cash Allocation
detail: The need
A sum voted each year by a body that already meets and already has a budget.
How it differs from multi-year
It is not guaranteed beyond the current year, but the decision is made by people who know the club -- so renewal is a conversation rather than an application.
Worked figure
A PTA allocation in the $300-$800 range is typical, and it usually arrives faster than any grant.

nodes.label:
Cross-Promotion to
Local Families
detail: The need
Reaching families who would join if they knew the club existed.
Why it belongs on a funding map
It is not cash, and it changes the same numbers: more families is more fee income under a sliding scale, and a stronger case in every future grant application.
Note
The cheapest need to meet on this map, and the one clubs ask for last.

nodes.label:
Community
Foundation Grant
detail: What it is
A local grant-making body that exists to fund community organisations, often with multi-year programmes.
What it addresses
The only partner here that can commit money beyond a single year.
The cost
The heaviest application of the four -- a written proposal, a budget, and usually a reporting obligation afterwards.

nodes.label:
School District
Funding
detail: What it is
A partnership with the district that most often takes the form of space rather than cash.
What it addresses
A room, after hours, at no charge -- and sometimes the caretaking and insurance that come with it.
The catch
District space usually comes with district rules: safeguarding checks, term-time only, and a calendar you do not control.

nodes.label:
PTA Partnership
Funding
detail: What it is
An allocation voted by the parent-teacher association, typically annually.
What it addresses
Renewable cash, decided by people who already know the club and can see the students in it.
Why it is the fastest
No formal application in most cases -- a short presentation at a meeting, and a vote.

nodes.label:
Library Funding
Partnership
detail: What it is
A relationship with a public library, which usually has meeting rooms, a mailing list, and a mandate to host community learning.
What it addresses
Space AND promotion -- the only partner on this map that meets two different needs from one relationship.
Why that matters
One conversation, two problems solved. It is the highest return per hour of any partnership here, and the one most often overlooked because it does not arrive as money.

legend.text: Every arrow reads "need is addressed by partner"
